It then applies graph-based community detection to create a thematic partitioning of the data.","citationIds":["c1"]},{"text":"**RAG basics:** RAG means a user query is used to retrieve relevant information from external data sources, and that information is incorporated into the LLM's response generation. The query and retrieved records populate a prompt template. RAG is ideal when the data source has too many records to fit in a single prompt.","citationIds":["c2"]},{"text":"**How the Microsoft GraphRAG approach works:** It uses summaries over large sections of the data as a form of \"self-memory\". These summaries are generated in parallel and iteratively aggregated into global summaries. They are later used to answer queries.","citationIds":["c1"]},{"text":"**Reported performance:** In the Microsoft paper, GraphRAG strongly outperforms vector RAG on real-world text datasets when GPT-4 is the LLM.","citationIds":["c2"]},{"text":"**Availability:** GraphRAG is open source (github.com/microsoft/graphrag). Versions also exist as extensions to LangChain, LlamaIndex, NebulaGraph, and Neo4J.","citationIds":["c2"]},{"text":"**General framework (survey view):** A holistic GraphRAG framework has five components: query processor, retriever, organizer, generator, and graph data source. Another section of the same survey lists the components as graph construction, retriever, organizer, generator, and data source.","citationIds":["c3","c4"]},{"text":"**Domains:** The survey categorizes GraphRAG designs into 10 domains, including knowledge graph, document graph, scientific graph, social graph, planning & reasoning graph, and tabular graph.","citationIds":["c3"]},{"text":"**Comparison with VectorRAG and HybridRAG (one financial-document study):** Faithfulness was 0.96 for GraphRAG and HybridRAG versus 0.94 for VectorRAG. Answer relevancy was highest for HybridRAG at 0.96, then VectorRAG at 0.91 and GraphRAG at 0.89. Context precision was highest for GraphRAG at 0.96, ahead of VectorRAG (0.84) and HybridRAG (0.79).","citationIds":["c5"]},{"text":"**Cost caveat (from the LightRAG paper):** LightRAG compares its cost with GraphRAG's. In the retrieval phase, GraphRAG uses about 610 × 1,000 tokens, while LightRAG uses fewer than 100.","citationIds":["c6"]},{"text":"**Open challenge:** Adapting GraphRAG to new fields requires understanding each domain's requirements, data structures, and graph configurations.
